title: Property overrides
description: Hand-authored corrections and additions applied on top of properties extracted from Redpanda's C++ source. See tools/property-extractor/README.adoc.

properties.description: Keyed by property key or name (see property_extractor.py's name-fallback lookup). An override key that matches neither creates a phantom stub property — see property_extractor.py's report_phantom_stubs().

_comment.description: Free-text note to whoever edits this entry next. Never read by the generator.

description.description: Property description. A plain string, or an array of paragraphs when one of them belongs to a single docs build: an array entry may carry a 'cloud-only:' / 'self-managed-only:' prefix and the generator wraps it in the matching ifdef::env-cloud[] conditional. Prefer the array form over writing the conditional into the string, because the overrides audit can only compare prose it can separate from markup, so a hand-written conditional pins the override forever.

links.description: Inline links, keyed by the literal text to find in the prose (backticks included, as written) and valued by the target. Only the first occurrence of a key is linked, and the longest key wins. Two target forms: '#<property_name>' emits a prop macro, which resolves the reference page itself and renders plain code in a build that does not publish the target, so it needs no conditional and cannot dangle; 'xref:<target>' emits a literal xref with the key as its link text; 'glossterm' wraps the key in a glossary tooltip (use 'glossterm:<Term>' when the prose says something other than the term's own name). A target may carry a 'cloud-only:' / 'self-managed-only:' prefix, in which case the containing paragraph is emitted twice: linked in that branch, plain in the other. Keeping links here rather than in the sentence is what lets the description stay prose the audit can compare against the source string.

includes.description: Shared partials pulled into this property's entry, as Antora resource IDs (for example reference:partial$internal-use-property.adoc). Rendered as include:: directives immediately after the description, which is where they used to be written by hand. Keeping them here rather than inside the description string is what lets the prose stay comparable to the source doc string. An entry may carry a 'cloud-only:' / 'self-managed-only:' prefix, and its own [attrs] if it needs them.

upstream_ref.description: The upstream issue or PR (against the engineering repo whose defective string this description patches, either the short form 'redpanda-data/streaming-enterprise#12345' or the full URL) that will make this description override redundant once merged and released. A description override is a stopgap, not a fix: set this so the override is born with a retirement path, and remove both the override and this field once the fix ships. Only meaningful alongside 'description' — has no effect on generation or rendering.

version.description: Version the property was introduced in (e.g. 'v23.1.0').

example.description: Literal example content, or an example_file/example_yaml reference resolved relative to this overrides file.

default.description: Replaces the extracted default. Prefer leaving this unset — it silently pins a value the extractor would otherwise keep in sync with the C++ source on every release.

config_scope.description: Almost always inferred automatically from defined_in — see property_extractor.py's add_config_scope(). Only set this for an override-created property (defined_in: 'override'), which has no source file to infer from.

category.description: Documentation grouping. Not inferable for cluster/broker properties; topic properties get a mechanical default from infer_category() that this can still override.

accepted_values.description: Replaces the enum field to filter displayed values (e.g. hiding an internal-only mode).

related_topics.description: Deprecated — use see_also. A plain string, or one prefixed 'cloud-only:'/'self-managed-only:' for conditional display. The prefix is free text with no validation; still read for existing entries, normalized alongside see_also by seeAlsoView.js.

see_also.description: Related commands or documentation pages. Each item is a plain string (shown everywhere) or an object naming exactly one of cloud_only/self_managed_only (shown only in that build). Same shape as rpk-overrides.json's 'seeAlso', except that file spells the flags in camelCase to match its own key style.

oneOf.description: xref link or related-topic text, shown in every build.
Conditional see-also item shown only in the named build.

content.description: The xref link or related-topic text.

cloud_only.description: If true, only shown in Cloud docs (wrapped with ifdef::env-cloud[]). Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

self_hosted_only.description: Deprecated spelling of self_managed_only. Still read, so an override written against the older schema keeps working, but nothing emits it. Use self_managed_only. Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

self_managed_only.description: If true, only shown in self-managed docs (wrapped with ifndef::env-cloud[]). Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

admonitions.description: Structured NOTE/TIP/IMPORTANT/WARNING/CAUTION callouts, rendered as Asciidoctor admonition blocks instead of hand-written markup in description. Each entry needs type and text; title is optional. See property_extractor.py's _normalize_admonitions() -- an entry that doesn't match this shape is dropped with a warning, not rejected here, so the schema stays permissive on casing/whitespace that the generator itself normalizes.

type.description: Case-insensitive; normalized to uppercase. One of note, tip, important, warning, caution.

text.description: Admonition body. May itself contain AsciiDoc markup.

title.description: Optional admonition title, shown in place of the default type label.

cloud_only.description: Show this admonition only in the Cloud build (wrapped with ifdef::env-cloud[]). Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

self_managed_only.description: Show this admonition only in the self-managed build (wrapped with ifndef::env-cloud[]). Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

self_hosted_only.description: Deprecated spelling of self_managed_only. Still read, so an override written against the older schema keeps working, but nothing emits it: the product is Self-Managed and the string prefix has always been 'self-managed-only:', so one concept was going by two words depending on whether you wrote it as a prefix or a boolean. Use self_managed_only. Only `true` is accepted: the emitters test for exactly true, so `false` behaves as if the key were absent while reading as though it meant the opposite audience. Omit the key instead.

not.$comment: Setting both audiences would wrap the block in ifdef and ifndef at once, so it would render in neither build. Only an exact true counts, so cloud_only: false beside self_managed_only: true stays valid.
Same check against the deprecated spelling.
